review_candidates.title: Senior Corporate Counsel, Licensing & Business Contracts - Peru - Fully Remote
review_candidates.description: Description Ranked in the Top 20 of the Forbes Best-In-State Companies in 2026, Sun World International is a California-based agriculture and technology firm engaged in fruit variety development, technology, intellectual property, and licensing. Technology and IP pursuits include one of the world’s leading fruit breeding/genetics programs, a broad-based portfolio of plant patents and trademarks and investments in agriculture technology start-ups benefiting its global licensees. The Company prizes creativity, innovation, and an entrepreneurial spirit. Its people strive for excellence by demonstrating leadership, passion, kindness, authenticity, courage, initiative, and curiosity. The Senior Corporate Counsel, Licensing & Business Contracts is a senior member of the Legal & Intellectual Property team and leads the company’s licensing and business contracts function. The role provides practical, commercially focused legal support across the organization, with primary responsibility for the negotiation, drafting, administration, and governance of licensing and other commercial agreements. This position works closely with commercial, finance, operations, research and development, intellectual property, and executive teams across multiple jurisdictions. The Senior Corporate Counsel also manages and develops the team within the unit, establishes consistent contracting practices, and helps ensure that contractual arrangements protect the company’s intellectual property, support its business strategy, and can be implemented effectively. Key Responsibilities Licensing and Business Contracts Lead the drafting, review, negotiation, amendment, renewal, and termination of licensing and other commercial agreements, including grower, nursery, marketer, distributor, trial, evaluation, research, services, procurement, confidentiality, technology, consulting, and strategic partnership agreements. Advise on the structure of complex and cross-border licensing arrangements involving plant variety rights, patents, trademarks, proprietary plant material, know-how, royalties, territory, exclusivity, quality requirements, production, distribution, and enforcement rights. Translate business objectives into clear, practical, and enforceable contractual terms, while identifying material legal and commercial risks and proposing workable solutions. Support business teams throughout the contract lifecycle, from initial term sheets and approvals through execution, implementation, amendment, renewal, and exit. Ensure that contractual rights and obligations are consistent across related agreements and aligned with the company’s intellectual property strategy, commercial model, and operational capabilities. Manage contractual disputes, defaults, and performance issues in coordination with internal stakeholders and, when appropriate, outside counsel. Business Partnership and Legal Advice Serve as a trusted legal partner to senior leaders and business teams, providing timely, clear, and solutions-oriented advice on commercial transactions and day-to-day business matters. Advise on contract interpretation, authority and approval requirements, competition and antitrust considerations, data protection, compliance, and other legal issues arising from commercial arrangements. Participate in strategic projects, new market initiatives, acquisitions, collaborations, and business-model development, particularly where licensing or intellectual property is central to the transaction. Coordinate with local counsel in relevant jurisdictions and manage outside counsel efficiently, including scope, budget, quality, and delivery of advice. Team Leadership and Unit Management Lead, supervise, and develop the lawyers, contract professionals, paralegals, and administrative team members assigned to the Licensing & Business Contracts unit. Set priorities, allocate work, monitor workload and performance, and ensure that matters are handled efficiently and at the appropriate level. Provide substantive guidance, quality control, coaching, and professional development to team members, while promoting accountability, sound judgment, and a strong service mindset. Establish clear service standards, workflows, and escalation protocols for the unit, and report on workload, priorities, risks, and performance to the Vice President, Legal & Intellectual Property. Build effective working relationships across the Legal & IP department and ensure smooth coordination with the intellectual property administration, enforcement, compliance, and legal operations functions. Contract Governance and Legal Operations Develop, maintain, and improve contract templates, clause libraries, negotiation playbooks, approval matrices, policies, and guidance materials. Promote consistent use of the company’s contract management processes and systems, including intake, review, approval, signature, storage, obligation tracking, renewal, and reporting. Identify recurring contractual and operational risks, recommend process improvements, and help implement scalable solutions that improve quality and turnaround time. Support training for business teams on contracting practices, delegated authority, licensing requirements, intellectual property protection, and other relevant legal topics. Maintain appropriate records and contribute to reporting on contract activity, key obligations, risk areas, and departmental performance. Requirements Juris Doctor or equivalent law degree from an accredited institution and active membership in good standing with an applicable bar or law society. At least eight years of relevant legal experience, including substantial responsibility for commercial contracting and licensing matters; a combination of in-house and law-firm experience is preferred. Of note: For those with in-house experience, the successful candidate will be required to have experience working for a global organization. A minimum of 3 years of demonstrated experience leading, supervising, or developing legal and contract professionals, with the ability to manage competing priorities across a busy global portfolio. Strong drafting and negotiation skills, with experience handling complex, high-value, and cross-border agreements. Willingness to travel up to 20% of the time. Preferences Experience advising a global agricultural, life sciences, food, biotechnology, consumer-products, or intellectual-property-driven business is preferred. Experience with intellectual property licensing—particularly plant variety rights, patents, trademarks, proprietary materials, or technology—is highly desirable. Professional fluency in written and spoken English is required. Professional proficiency in Spanish is strongly preferred, including the ability to review and negotiate agreements and communicate effectively with Spanish-speaking stakeholders. Work schedule: 100% remote - any location within Peru.

This is a core leadership role that bridges technical execution, subcontractor management, and client quality acceptance. Key Responsibilities Develop, update, and implement project QA/QC plans, inspection checklists, quality procedures, and work instructions in line with ISO 9001, project specs, and industry standards. Lead and manage the on-site QA/QC team, allocate daily inspection tasks, supervise inspectors’ field work, and conduct regular team training to standardize quality execution. Oversee full-cycle civil construction quality control, including foundation works, concrete works, steel structure, backfilling, roadworks, drainage, and finishing works; conduct random and systematic on-site inspections, testing witnessing, and progress quality verification. Monitor construction quality of subcontractors, conduct regular quality audits, track non-conformities, organize root cause analysis, and drive corrective & preventive actions (CAPA) to eliminate recurring quality issues. Prepare, review, and submit all QA/QC documentation, including inspection reports, test reports, material approval documents, non-conformance reports, and daily/weekly/monthly quality progress reports for client and consultant review. Coordinate with clients, consultants, project management teams, and third-party testing institutions to resolve on-site quality queries and ensure smooth quality acceptance and handover. Control material quality incoming inspection, verify material certificates, and ensure all construction materials comply with project design and specification requirements. Support internal and external quality audits, summarize project quality performance, and continuously optimize on-site quality management systems and processes. Job Requirements & Qualifications Education : Bachelor’s degree in Civil Engineering, Construction Management or related engineering disciplines. Experience : 8+ years of hands-on QA/QC experience in civil construction projects, with minimum 3 years of QA/QC manager experience. Professional Knowledge : Proficient in international construction codes & standards, civil construction workmanship requirements, material testing procedures, and full set of QA/QC document management workflows. Certifications : Possession of ISO 9001 internal auditor certificate or other relevant construction quality certificates is highly preferred. Core Competencies : Strong on-site problem-solving ability, familiar with subcontractor quality management, capable of independently handling client quality inspections and audits. Language & Skill : Good English listening, speaking and writing skills (for overseas project communication); proficient in MS Office, quality report preparation and data sorting. Personal Traits : Strict, responsible, detail-oriented, with strong team management, communication and cross-department coordination capabilities.
